text.p: Russian oil company AO Yuganskneftegaz is undervalued but not yet attractive, U.S. investment bank Salomon Bros said on Thursday, reiterating its hold recommendation.
It said it had steadily downgraded the share since March because of several concerns, including:
- lack of clarity regarding the terms of conversion into vertically-integrated company and parent YUKOS;
- Yuganskneftegaz has been run since August as a cost centre and cash flows are being depressed to suit YUKOS;
- overdue tax liabilities have risen to $546 million from $532 million in June;
- progress with Yuganskneftegaz's most attractive asset for future growth -- the North Priobsk oil field -- is being held up.
"Despite an increase in our overall valuation of Yugansk and the increase in the value gap in the stock market, we do not recommend buying Yugansk's shares," Salomon said.
The argument that Yuganskneftegaz offers a way into YUKOS assumes that the share conversion does take place and no alternative investment route into YUKOS appears, it noted.

Bank Menatep, which controls 85 percent of YUKOS, has designed and is implementing a restructuring programme for Yuganskneftegaz. It has taken control of Yuganskneftegaz's budget and running it as a cost centre for YUKOS even before the conversion.

"Menatep and YUKOS already control almost 100 percent of sales and distribution of Yugansk's crude at prices which appear to favour refining and marketing subsidiaries and could result in losses for Yugansk," it said.
Menatep is selling one third of YUKOS next month.
